 The worst weather may be over, but Highway 1 in Big Sur remains closed

 Caltrans crews work to remove downed trees and remove rocks from Highway 1 after the storm brought heavy winds and rain to the area. More than 1200 are without power as the rainy weather is expected to continue. (Photos courtesy of Caltrans District 5) 
 By Kyarra Harris | kharris@montereyherald.com PUBLISHED: November 19, 2026 at 2:34 PM PST | UPDATED: November 19, 2026 at 2:56 PM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... MONTEREY — Meteorologists with the National Weather Service say the worst of this current bout of bad weather is behind us, but Monterey County can expect more rain in coming days.
 Heavy rain triggered rockslides, mudslides and debris flow onto Highway 1 in Big Sur, causing officials to close a 46-mile stretch from Nepenthe to Ragged Point. A Flash Flood Warning had been issued Wednesday afternoon for the areas near Timber and Plaskett burn scars.
 Many other areas of the county dealt with power outages, with more than 1,200 being affected.
 On Carmel Point, many areas of Scenic Road were closed as the County of Monterey’s Engineering team determined that a segment of the roadway “has been compromised by wave action,” according to the county. Due to the structural damage and additional high surf expected later this week, the roadway is closed until further notice.
 Friday through Sunday, the rain is expected to continue, although the weather cleared for portion of the day Thursday, with consistent light rain.
 Two advisories were in place Thursday morning. The flash flood watch is expected to end late afternoon Thursday, while the high surf advisory was to remain in effect until 1 a.m. on Friday.
 The high surf advisory warns of large breaking waves that can overpower swimmers, pull people into the sea from beaches, jetties and rocks, and can result in significant physical injury or increase the risk of drowning.
 Highway 1 along the Big Sur coast was closed overnight Nov. 18 due to debris flows, flooding, and rocks in the roadway. Caltrans crews are onsite clearing multiple locations. (Photo courtesy of Caltrans District 5) 
 Monterey Peninsula cities are also monitoring beach entrances and coastal hotspots like Del Monte Beach in Seaside, and the coast along Ocean View Boulevard in Pacific Grove. First responders have been on the scene telling people to get away from the water due to high surf.
 The County of Monterey is tracking road closures and updates to the weather at readymontereycounty.org/emergency/2026-winter-storms . Residents can also receive emergency alerts from Alert Monterey County by texting your zip code to 65513 or sign up online at alertmontereycounty.org.
